subject: math.NT
name: Riemann hypothesis
statement: Every nontrivial zero of the analytically continued Riemann zeta function ζ(s) has real part 1/2.
importance: Controls the finest expected error bounds in the distribution of prime numbers.
status_note: Computations and partial zero-density results do not establish the assertion for every nontrivial zero.

subject: math.NT
name: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer conjecture
statement: For every elliptic curve E over Q, the order of vanishing of its L-function L(E,s) at s=1 equals the rank of the finitely generated group E(Q).
importance: Relates analytic behavior to the arithmetic abundance of rational points.
status_note: Important analytic-rank-zero and rank-one cases are known; the rank equality for arbitrary elliptic curves remains open.

references.title: Clay Mathematics Institute: Birch and Swinnerton-Dyer Conjecture

subject: math.NT
name: Twin prime conjecture
statement: There are infinitely many primes p for which p+2 is also prime.
importance: The simplest fixed-gap prediction for the distribution of primes.
status_note: Bounded gaps between primes are proved, but an infinitely recurring gap of exactly 2 is not.

subject: math.NT
name: Strong Goldbach conjecture
statement: Every even integer greater than 2 is the sum of two prime numbers, with repetition allowed.
importance: A foundational additive-prime problem whose elementary statement has resisted centuries of work.
status_note: The three-prime weak Goldbach theorem is proved; the two-prime assertion remains open.

subject: math.NT
name: Schanuel conjecture
statement: For complex numbers z₁,…,z_n linearly independent over Q, the field Q(z₁,…,z_n,e^z₁,…,e^z_n) has transcendence degree at least n over Q.
importance: Would unify major algebraic-independence predictions in transcendental number theory.
status_note: This is a conjecture about the usual complex exponential function; related results for special arguments do not prove it.

subject: math.NT
name: Lehmer’s Mahler-measure problem
statement: Is there a constant c>1 such that every nonzero algebraic integer α that is not a root of unity has Mahler measure at least c? For its monic minimal polynomial with roots α_i, the measure is ∏_i max(1,|α_i|).
importance: Asks for a universal gap in the arithmetic complexity of algebraic numbers.
status_note: Bounds depending on the degree are known; a degree-independent gap above 1 remains open.

subject: math.NT
name: Lang–Trotter conjecture
statement: For a non-CM elliptic curve E over Q and a fixed integer r, the number of good primes p≤x with p+1−#E(F_p)=r is asymptotic to C(E,r)√x/log x when the predicted constant C(E,r)>0.
importance: Predicts fine statistics of Frobenius traces beyond broad equidistribution theorems.
status_note: The non-CM and positive-constant hypotheses exclude different asymptotics and arithmetic obstructions.

subject: math.NT
name: Littlewood conjecture
statement: For every pair of real numbers α,β, liminf as n→∞ of n·||nα||·||nβ|| equals 0, where ||x|| is the distance from x to the nearest integer.
importance: A central simultaneous Diophantine-approximation problem with links to dynamics.
status_note: The conjecture is known for many pairs; strong bounds on the exceptional set do not show it is empty.

subject: math.NT
name: Bunyakovsky conjecture
statement: Every irreducible polynomial f∈Z[x] of positive degree with positive leading coefficient and no prime dividing f(n) for every integer n takes positive prime values at infinitely many positive integers.
importance: Extends prime values in arithmetic progressions to nonlinear polynomials.
status_note: Degree one follows from Dirichlet’s theorem; no general theorem covers degree two, including n²+1.

subject: math.NT
name: Generalized Ramanujan–Petersson conjecture
statement: Every unitary cuspidal automorphic representation of GL_n over a number field is tempered at every unramified finite place; equivalently, its normalized unramified Satake parameters all have absolute value 1.
importance: A central size bound for automorphic forms that drives analytic-number-theory estimates.
status_note: Major special cases are proved, including holomorphic modular forms; general Maass forms and higher-rank representations remain unresolved.
